cards.front: What is matter?
cards.back: Anything that has mass and occupies space
cards.explain: Air, water, food and even our body are matter.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Air is not matter because we cannot see it.

blank.text: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies ___.

cards.front: What are the tiny particles that matter is made of?
cards.explain: Matter is made of molecules, and molecules are made of even tinier atoms.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is the basic building block of all matter?
cards.explain: Two or more atoms join together to form a molecule.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Atoms can be seen with the naked eye.

blank.text: Two or more ___ join together to form a molecule.

cards.front: What is the space between two molecules called?
cards.explain: It is smallest in solids and largest in gases.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is the amount of matter in a body called?
cards.explain: The amount of space an object occupies is its volume.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is the amount of space an object occupies called?
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What are the three states of matter?
cards.explain: The difference between them lies in how their molecules are arranged.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: In which state of matter are molecules most tightly packed?
cards.explain: Strong attraction holds the molecules of a solid close together, so they cannot move.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: In solids, the molecules are loosely packed.

blank.text: In ___, the molecules are tightly packed.

cards.front: In which state is the force of attraction between molecules the least?
cards.explain: Gas molecules have a lot of free space and move freely in all directions.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Why does a solid have a fixed shape and size?
cards.back: Its molecules are tightly packed and cannot move
cards.explain: Strong attraction keeps the molecules in place.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Solids can be compressed easily.

cards.front: Why do liquids flow?
cards.explain: Liquid molecules are more loosely packed than in solids, so they slide past each other.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: Liquids flow from a ___ level to a lower level.

cards.front: A liquid has a fixed volume. Does it have a fixed shape?
cards.back: No – it takes the shape of its container
cards.explain: Water in a glass and in a bottle has different shapes but the same volume.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: No – and no fixed volume either

tf.text: Liquids have a fixed volume but no fixed shape.

cards.front: Which state of matter can be compressed to a large extent?
cards.explain: Gases have lots of free space between molecules – that is why we can fill so much air into a balloon or tyre.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is solubility?
cards.back: The ability of a substance to dissolve in another substance
cards.explain: Sugar has high solubility in water.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: The ability to float on water

cards.front: The substance that dissolves is called the …?
cards.explain: In salt water, salt is the solute.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: A substance that dissolves in another substance is called a ___.

cards.front: The substance in which the solute dissolves is called the …?
cards.explain: In salt water, water is the solvent.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Salt + water gives salt water. What is salt water called?
cards.explain: Solute + solvent = solution.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What is a uniform solution?
cards.back: A solution where the solute spreads evenly through the solvent
cards.explain: Salt breaks into molecules that spread evenly between the water molecules.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: A solution with lumps at the bottom
A solution that cannot be poured

cards.front: Sand, chalk powder and tea leaves do not dissolve in water. What are they called?
cards.explain: Salt and sugar, which dissolve, are soluble substances.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Sugar is an insoluble substance.

cards.front: Liquids that dissolve easily in water, like milk, are called …?
cards.explain: Milk, glycerine and alcohol are miscible with water.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Oil floats on water and does not mix. Oil is a … liquid.
cards.explain: Oil and petrol are immiscible with water.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Oil is miscible in water.

cards.front: Why do bubbles come out when we open a bottle of soda?
cards.back: Carbon dioxide dissolved under pressure escapes
cards.explain: Soda has carbon dioxide dissolved in it under high pressure – this gives the fizz.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: Oxygen is made inside the bottle

tf.text: Carbon dioxide does not dissolve in water.

cards.front: How do fish breathe under water?
cards.back: They use oxygen dissolved in water
cards.explain: Gases like oxygen and carbon dioxide dissolve in water. Aquatic plants use the dissolved carbon dioxide to make food.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: They come up for air every minute

cards.front: Why is water called the universal solvent?
cards.back: It can dissolve more substances than any other liquid
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: Water is known as the universal ___.

cards.front: A solid changing into a liquid on heating is called …?
cards.explain: Ice melting into water is an example.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Melting of ice is a chemical change.

cards.front: A liquid changing into a gas on heating is called …?
cards.explain: Wet clothes dry because the water evaporates.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: A liquid changing into a solid on cooling is called …?
cards.explain: Water kept in the freezer turns into ice.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: Water kept in the freezer turns into ice. This is called ___.

cards.front: A gas changing into a liquid on cooling is called …?
cards.explain: Water drops form outside a cold glass because water vapour in the air condenses. Dew forms the same way.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: What happens to the molecules of a substance when it is heated?
cards.back: They gain energy and move faster
cards.explain: On cooling, molecules lose energy and slow down.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: They lose energy and slow down

tf.text: The movement of molecules increases on cooling.

cards.front: Most solids get bigger when heated. What is this called?
cards.explain: On cooling, solids contract (get smaller) as their molecules come closer.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

blank.text: Most solids ___ on heating and contract on cooling.

cards.front: What is a physical change?
cards.back: A temporary change where no new substance is formed
cards.explain: It is usually reversible, like water ↔ ice.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: A permanent change that forms a new substance
A change that can never be reversed
A change only in living things

tf.text: Physical change is a permanent change.

cards.front: What is a chemical change?
cards.back: A permanent change where new substances are formed
cards.explain: Burning leaves gives ash, which is very different from leaves.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: A temporary change with no new substance
A change that is easy to reverse

blank.text: A change that produces new substances is called a ___ change.

cards.front: Melting chocolate in a pan – physical or chemical change?
cards.explain: The melted chocolate can set again – no new substance is formed.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Baking a cookie – physical or chemical change?
cards.explain: Baked dough cannot turn back into raw dough – new substances form.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Rusting of an iron nail – physical or chemical change?
cards.explain: Rust is a new substance and the change cannot be reversed.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

tf.text: Rusting of iron is a chemical change.

cards.front: Making a boat from paper – physical or chemical change?
cards.explain: Only the shape changes; you can unfold it back.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: Burning a candle involves which kind of change?
cards.explain: Wax melting is physical; wax burning to give heat, light and gases is chemical.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1

cards.front: How does the smell of food cooking in the kitchen spread through the whole house?
cards.back: Gas molecules move freely in all directions
cards.explain: The aroma is carried by gas molecules that spread out to fill the space.
cards.source: Collins Class 5 Science, Ch 1
wrong: The smell travels through the walls

cards.front: What is the blanket of air around the Earth called?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which gas makes up most of the air?
cards.explain: About 78% of air is nitrogen and about 21% is oxygen.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

tf.text: Oxygen is the gas found most in air.

cards.front: Which gas in air do we need to breathe?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which gas do plants take in to make food?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: The lowest layer of the atmosphere, where we live, is the …?
cards.explain: Weather happens in this layer.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which layer protects us from the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays?
cards.explain: It is in the stratosphere.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.explain: Air also has weight and exerts pressure.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: About how much of the Earth's surface is covered with water?
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Letting mud settle at the bottom of a glass of water is called …?
cards.explain: Pouring off the clear water after that is decantation.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Which method kills germs in water at home?
cards.explain: Water is also cleaned with chlorine tablets (chlorination).

cards.explain: Granite and basalt are igneous rocks.

cards.front: Rocks formed from layers of sand, mud and pebbles pressed together are …?
cards.explain: Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary rocks.

cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Marble is formed from which rock?
cards.explain: The Taj Mahal is made of marble.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: What is the hardest mineral?
cards.explain: Talc is the softest mineral.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Hot liquid rock inside the Earth is called …?
cards.explain: When it comes out of a volcano it is called lava.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: Rocks from which metals are taken out are called …?
cards.explain: Iron is taken out of iron ore.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.explain: Weathering of rocks forms soil.
cards.source: Class 5 topic, written from the Collins chapter title

cards.front: मुफ़्तलाल ने गाँव के चारों ओर क्या लगाया?
cards.explain: वे सोचते थे – "जब पेड़ बड़े हो जाएँगे तो सारे फल मुझे खाने को मिला करेंगे… मुफ़्त में ही मैं धनवान बन जाऊँगा।"
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, Ch 10 (pp. 96–105)

cards.front: कोमलपुर गाँव किस कारण चर्चित होने लगा?
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, Ch 10 (pp. 96–105)

cards.front: पर्यावरण विभाग ने कोमलपुर के मुफ़्तलाल को क्या दिया?
cards.explain: पर्यावरण में उत्कृष्ट योगदान के लिए उन्हें पुरस्कार दिया गया।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, Ch 10 (pp. 96–105)

blank.text: एक दिन पर्यावरण विभाग के कुछ लोगों ने कोमलपुर के मुफ़्तलाल को ___ दिया।

cards.front: आज भी गाँव के लोग मुफ़्तलाल को श्रद्धांजलि कैसे देते हैं?
cards.back: वन महोत्सव पर एक-एक पेड़ लगाकर
cards.explain: मुफ़्तलाल गाँववालों को अपार वृक्ष-संपदा सौंपकर परलोक सिधार गए।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, Ch 10 (pp. 96–105)

cards.front: इस पाठ से हमें क्या सीख मिलती है?
cards.back: पेड़ों की उपयोगिता पहचानना और पर्यावरण के प्रति सचेत रहना
cards.explain: मैंने सीखा: लालच से दूर रहना, पेड़ों की उपयोगिता पहचानना, समाजोपयोगी कार्य करना।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, Ch 10 (pp. 96–105)
wrong: हर चीज़ मुफ़्त में लेनी चाहिए

cards.back: मुफ़्त सिनेमा और मुफ़्त फलदार पेड़ की बात कहकर उन्हें फ़िल्म में भेजा
cards.explain: वह मुफ़्तलाल की मानसिकता से अच्छी तरह परिचित था।
cards.source: Class 5 Hindi book, Ch 10 (pp. 96–105)

cards.back: मुफ़्त फल पाने के लिए पेड़ लगाने में, जिससे गाँव हरा-भरा हो गया

cards.back: मुफ़्तलाल के लगाए पेड़ों में फल लगने के लिए
cards.explain: मेहनत रंग लाना = किसी काम में सफल होना।
